conventions.deferred:: A real obligation this plan carries; the suffix names the milestone whose scope in PLAN.md the clause falls in — S5 for the messaging layer, which owns this doc. The note names the gap that keeps the clause out of the carrier set. An entry with this value says that nothing under lean/ or vectors/ carries the clause's requirement: a missing carrier is recorded rather than covered by naming a declaration that does not hold the rule.
conventions.formalized:: A Lean declaration path that carries this clause's meaning. Every path recorded here names a declaration the module it names actually holds, and the ledger's existence gate resolves it against lean/** rather than taking the note's word for it.
conventions.kind: The clause's own keyword, read from the ledger's clause rather than inferred from the coverage class: the class is MUST for both forms, so kind and class diverge for MUST NOT. Two of this file's clauses are the MUST NOT half of a sentence whose MUST half is keyed beside them.
conventions.test:: A vector id whose verdict is the clause's observable form; the ledger's vector gate resolves every id recorded here against vectors/**.

design_consequences: This doc is the artifact's worked resumption example, and it is the one place the resumption family's obligations are stated as MUSTs rather than as narrative: the sender resends, does not set `resume` when the receiver has no record, does set it when the receiver has a record but no data, and restates a terminal outcome the receiver asks for.

Ten of its eleven must-class clauses are uncarried and one is carried, and the split is the model's shape rather than the doc's subject: the carried one (`.15`) is a law about a *delivery state* — terminal states do not change — which the message layer's machine implements and 27 vectors cite, while the other ten are obligations on a *sender* acting over an unsettled map, and this model has no sender and no map.

Four of the ten are two sentences keyed twice each (`.1`/`.2` and `.12`/`.13`), because each sentence contains both a MUST and a MUST NOT: the ledger's keyword split makes two clauses of one statement, which is the relationship sessions.3/.4 already have.

amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:mes.clause_text: To preserve "exactly once" or "at least once" delivery guarantees, the sender MUST resend the message; however, the delivery is not being resumed (since the receiver does not remember the delivery tag) so transfers MUST NOT have the resume flag set to true.
amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:mes.note: deferred: S5 — uncarried: the sender's side of link recovery: which deliveries it resends, from where, and whether the resending transfer carries `resume`. The model has no sending side and no unsettled map — `Session` holds one delivery in progress rather than a map from delivery-tags to states (lean/Spec/Session.lean:474), `transferLink` reads the transfer's `resume` field nowhere (lean/Spec/Session.lean:819-921), and `Contracts/Settlement.lean:185-189` records the restriction for exactly this family ('the clauses that talk about *entries* - resumption, in-doubt resolution, `unsettled`'s completeness - have no state to range over'). The receiver's half of the same rules is the links side's and is recorded there: `links/doc:resuming-deliveries.2` and `.8` name the same missing flag. The clause itself is one sentence carrying two obligations — the sender MUST resend, and transfers MUST NOT set `resume` — which the ledger keys as two clauses, `.1` for the MUST and `.2` for the MUST NOT; the same sentence is keyed again at `.12`/`.13` for the delivery-tag 5 case, so four clauses decide two statements. **And it is blocked rather than merely pending**: D4's fourth trigger — "a normative S5 clause the model cannot represent" — has fired on this family, so no clause batch reaches it until the model holds a link identity, an unsettled map and the sender's delivery bookkeeping. It is unreachable work rather than unfinished work.

amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:mes.clause_text: Once the sender has arrived at a terminal outcome it MUST NOT change.
amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:mes.note: A terminal delivery state is absorbing: `terminal_absorbing` states it over the machine that applies states (lean/Spec/Message.lean:1077-1084) — applying any state to a delivery whose state is terminal is refused — and `Contracts/Settlement.lean:37` cites this clause as the artifact's own MUST NOT of it. The vector that cites the clause pins a terminal outcome followed by another state, and the reading that settles the *neighbouring* question (settlement) is `ledger/ambiguities/settlement-is-absorbing.json`, which the same contract names.

amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:mes.clause_text: If the delivery-failed flag is set, any messages modified MUST have their delivery-count incremented.
amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:mes.note: The delivery-count's counting rule for `modified` is `incrementOf` (lean/Spec/Message.lean:995-998): a rejected outcome counts the attempt, a modified one counts it exactly when the peer said the delivery failed, and the other two outcomes state the opposite and are the reason this is a rule rather than a default. The vector cites the clause and pins the increment.

amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:mes.clause_text: If the undeliverable-here is set, then any messages released MUST NOT be redelivered to the modifying link endpoint.
amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:mes.note: The redelivery rule is `allowedOf` (lean/Spec/Message.lean:1003-1007): `accepted` retires the message, `rejected` makes it unprocessable, `released` makes it available again, and `modified` answers by its own `undeliverable-here` field — which is this sentence for the link it was modified at. The vector cites the clause.

amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:mes.clause_text: The sender MUST NOT send the «received» state on «transfer» or «disposition» performatives except on the first «transfer» performative on a resumed delivery.
amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:mes.note: deferred: S5 — uncarried: the sentence forbids sending the `received` state on a transfer or disposition except on the *first performative of a resumed delivery*, and the model has neither half of that condition: `deliveryStateOfValue` decodes and records a received state whenever a corpus supplies one (lean/Spec/Message.lean:940-969) and nothing reads a transfer's `resume` flag (lean/Spec/Session.lean:819-921), so 'the first performative of a resumed delivery' is not a position the session can be in. The near-miss is the state itself: the resume point is modelled and the restriction on when it may be sent is not.

amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:mes.clause_text: The message is unchanged at the node (i.e., the delivery-count of the header of the released message MUST NOT be incremented).
amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:mes.note: A released message does not increment the delivery-count, which is the third of the outcomes' counting rules in `incrementOf` (lean/Spec/Message.lean:995-998); the vector cites the clause and pins it against the `rejected` vector that does increment.
